cards.explanation: The answer is His Spirit, friends. The LORD says, "I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will bring justice to the nations." (Isaiah 42:1) The Servant doesn't go into this job alone or empty-handed. He starts with the LORD's own Spirit on Him.

The answer is False. Isaiah 42:2 says, "He will not cry out or raise His voice, nor make His voice heard in the streets." No megaphone, no hollering from the corner. The job is huge, and the Servant still goes about it quietly.

The answer is that He won't break them or snuff them out, friends. "A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish…" (Isaiah 42:3) Both of those are things that are barely holding on. I think that's a gentle picture. The verse goes on, "He will faithfully bring forth justice."

The answer is False. Isaiah 42:4 says, "He will not grow weak or discouraged before He has established justice on the earth." Most of us run out of steam on a Tuesday. The Servant doesn't run out before the job is finished.

The answer is the islands, friends. "In His law the islands will put their hope." (Isaiah 42:4) The islands are the ones who hope in His law. That comes right after the Servant will not grow weak or discouraged before He has established justice on the earth.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD is the One "…who gives breath to the people on it and life to those who walk in it…" (Isaiah 42:5) Every breath you took today came from Him. I'd say that is worth a thank you.

The answer is nations, friends. The LORD says He will appoint the one He called "…to be a covenant for the people and a light to the nations…" (Isaiah 42:6) The light isn't meant for one small corner. It reaches the nations.

The answer is to open the eyes of the blind, friends. The LORD names it in Isaiah 42:7, "…to open the eyes of the blind…" It's one of the jobs listed for the one He called. It sits right next to bringing prisoners out of the dungeon.

The answer is His praise, friends. The LORD says, "I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols." (Isaiah 42:8) His glory and His praise belong to Him. He won't hand either one to an idol.

The answer is new, friends. "Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things." (Isaiah 42:9) The former things have happened. Now the LORD is announcing something new. The verse adds, "Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you."
The answer is False. Isaiah 42:9 says, "Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you." He doesn't wait until the new things show up. He tells you ahead of time, before they spring forth.
